Kessel Optics Lenses assembled by hand in Pune.

Cinema and photography lenses. Three models. One optician builds each lens and signs the barrel.

Scroll to open the iris

01 · Iris

Light waits for the blades

The iris sits in the middle of the lens. Scroll and it opens one blade at a time until light floods the glass.

02 · Glass

Through the glass

Each element sits at its own distance from the next. Here they slide apart so the camera can pass between them, through the iris and out at the back.

03 · Back together

Out the back, closed up

Past the mount the camera turns round and the lens closes up behind it, element by element, until it is whole again.

04 · Focus

Focus by hand

The knurled ring turns and the engraved distance scale rolls past the index mark, from infinity down to the closest mark.

05 · Lenses

Three lenses

The names and roles below are proposals for this concept.

  1. Shaniwar proposal

    The wide one. For rooms, streets and landscapes, where everything in front of you belongs in the frame.

  2. Parvati proposal

    The standard one. Frames a scene close to the way your eye does.

  3. Sinhagad proposal

    The long one. For faces and details at a distance, with the background let go.

Craft

How a Kessel lens is made

Five stages, one pair of hands. Each lens is assembled by a single optician, from the first element to the signature on the barrel.

  1. 01

    Step 1: The glass

    Every element is cleaned and checked by eye before it goes into its cell. They are seated in the order the light will meet them, from the front of the lens to the back.

    The spacing between elements is part of the design, so each one is set at its own distance from the next before the stack is closed up.

  2. 02

    Step 2: The iris

    The blades go into the iris ring one at a time. Once they are in, the iris is run through its whole travel, from a pinhole to fully open, and watched for any blade that catches.

    The aperture ring that drives it is fitted afterwards and turned against the blades until the movement is even all the way round.

  3. 03

    Step 3: Barrel and focus ring

    The focus ring is fitted to the barrel and its engraved distance scale is checked against the index mark, so that what the ring says is where the lens is focused.

    The ring is meant to be turned by hand, take after take, so its weight and the evenness of its turn are checked as carefully as the scale.

  4. 04

    Step 4: Bringing it together

    The sections of the barrel are joined around the glass and the iris. Before the lens is closed for good, the whole optical stack is checked for alignment.

    This is the stage the film on the home page plays backwards: every part moving back into its place around the light path.

  5. 05

    Step 5: Signed on the barrel

    When the lens is finished, the optician who built it signs the barrel. One person, start to finish, and their mark stays on the lens.

    If a lens ever comes back to the workshop, the signature says whose hands it went through.

The workshop

A workshop in Pune

Kessel Optics is an independent lens maker, founded in Pune in 2017. It makes lenses for cinema and photography and assembles every one of them by hand.

Founded
2017
Workshop
Pune
Makes
Cinema and photography lenses
Range
Three lenses
Each lens
One optician, signed

01

Independent since 2017

Kessel Optics was founded in Pune in 2017. It is still an independent maker, and its range is deliberately small: three lenses, each with a clear job.

A small range means each lens can be built the same careful way every time, by hand, in one workshop.

02

One optician, one lens

Each lens is assembled from start to finish by one optician. The glass, the iris, the barrel and the focus ring all pass through the same pair of hands.

Nobody hands a half-finished lens down a line. The person who seats the first element is the person who closes the barrel.

03

Signed on the barrel

When a lens is finished, the optician who built it signs the barrel. It is the last thing that happens before the lens leaves the bench.

The signature is a record as much as a mark: it says who answers for that lens.
